answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake that grows with the value it transacts, like timber piled as collateral before a river crossing: creating one honest identity is cheap, but forging thousands becomes prohibitively expensive because every fake must post its own stake. Reputation then flows only through completed, attested work, and misbehavior slashes the stake, so an attacker crossing the tundra of fake accounts finds each step costs real capital while honest agents keep their deposits intact.
